chunks: And from him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ubayd ibn Hafs ibn Qurat Qurat, from Ismail ibn Jabir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! A bird falls upon the house, so it is seized. Is it permissible or prohibited for the one who seizes it?' So he said, 'O Ismail! Is it complete or not complete?' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! And what is complete?' He said, 'The one whose wings are level, in control of its wings, going wherever it desires.' He said, 'It is for the one who seizes it, permissible.'

key_terms.الْمُسْتَوِي جَنَاحَاهُ: The one whose wings are level/equal

ai.seo_question: Is a bird caught in the house considered halal or haram for the owner?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that a bird entering a home is lawful to keep if it is 'complete' (al-mustawi), meaning its wings are balanced and it retains the natural ability to fly away, distinguishing it from a weakened or captive specimen. This ruling, recorded in al-Kafi, establishes a practical criterion for ownership based on the animal's physical integrity and voluntary presence, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on clear, observable conditions in commercial and domestic transactions.

en.hubeali:
And from him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ubeyd Bin Hafs Bin Qurat, from Ismail Bin Jabir, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! The bird falls upon the house, so it is seized. Is it Permissible or Prohibited, for the one who seizes it?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Ismail! Is it complete or not complete (its wings)?’ I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! And what is complete?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who wings are level, in control of its wings going with them wherever it so desires to’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is for the one who seizes it’.
en.sarwar: 4. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from ibn Faddal from ‘Ubayd ibn Fiafs ibn al-Qurt from ’Isma‘il ibn Jabir who has said the following:

“I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, if a bird is trapped in the house and it is taken, is taking it lawful or unlawful. He (the Imam) asked, ‘O ’Isma‘il is it healthy or it is not healthy and free ? 5 I then asked, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, what is healthy ? 5 He (the Imam) said, ‘It is one with complete wings with full control on them and is able to fly wherever it wants . 5 He (the Imam) said, ‘Such ones belong to whoever catches them . 555
